comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides).
An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 — that script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions — so
nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file is what makes that check happen: on every run the script
executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to `expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different
means the condition that justified the pin has changed and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no
mechanical test exists — it is reported for manual review on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must
have an entry here, and every entry must correspond to a real pin; the script errors on either mismatch.
Prose rationale and the wider context live in AGENTS.md under 'Pinned versions'.

@codemirror/state.why: obsidian's peerDependencies names this exact version. A second copy in the tree means two CodeMirror state instances at runtime.

@codemirror/view.why: Same as @codemirror/state — obsidian peer-pins it exactly.

@lezer/common.why: Must match the copy Obsidian bundles at runtime: app.js registers '@lezer/common' in the module map it hands to plugins, so our copy is types-only and a newer pin would declare API the runtime lacks. Nothing else in the tree depends on it, so npm cannot detect or correct a mismatch. 1.5.2 was established by feature-marker comparison against Obsidian 1.13.4's app.js — see manualCheck. It replaced 1.2.3, which 1fdd8d24 had downgraded to from ^1.4.0 without a reason and which never matched the runtime.
@lezer/common.manualCheck: The check is a re-examination trigger, not proof: a newer publish means re-derive what Obsidian bundles, it does not by itself make the pin stale. The bundle embeds no version string, so derive it from feature markers — diff the dist of candidate versions (npm pack) and grep app.js for what distinguishes them. For 1.13.4: NodeProp 'combine' field and overlay 'depth++' after materialize => >=1.3.0; '-4 == size' (SpecialRecord.LookAhead) in the skipped-node scan => >=1.4.0; IterMode.EnterBracketed = 16 and MountedTree.bracketed => >=1.5.0; nextChild's bracketed test in the '!mounted.overlay && mounted.bracketed && pos >= start' form => >=1.5.1; FragmentCursor.moveTo guarding with 'cursor.to <= pos' => 1.5.2. Then run build:compile:typescript plus src/obsidian/editor.obsidian.integration.test.ts.

@puppeteer/browsers.why: Clears GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv (extract-zip unvalidated symlink path traversal, 7 high advisories) and nothing else. extract-zip is vulnerable at every published version, so there is no patched version to override it to, and the direct dependency cannot be bumped either: obsidian-integration-testing is already latest and pins webdriverio exactly, and even the newest webdriverio still reaches extract-zip through @wdio/utils -> @puppeteer/browsers ^2.x. @puppeteer/browsers@3 replaced extract-zip with modern-tar, so forcing 3.x on @wdio/utils - the only consumer left on 2.x - removes the subtree entirely. It also dedupes: puppeteer-core already brings 3.2.0 into this tree, so the override collapses two copies into one rather than adding anything. The major bump is safe because @wdio/utils imports only install, canDownload, resolveBuildId, detectBrowserPlatform, Browser, ChromeReleaseChannel, computeExecutablePath and the InstallOptions type, all still exported by 3.x with compatible signatures, and both packages are ESM-only. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy here: it downgrades obsidian-integration-testing from 12.x to 1.1.2, and a downgrade is never an acceptable way to clear an advisory.
@puppeteer/browsers.manualCheck: The check reads @wdio/utils's own declared range, not a version, because that range is what makes the override necessary. When it moves to ^3 or later, @wdio/utils no longer pulls extract-zip on its own and this override can be deleted along with this entry. A `require('@wdio/utils/package.json')` check would not work - its exports map does not expose package.json - hence the readFileSync form, which resolves relative to the package root the sweep runs from.

deepmerge-ts.why: Clears GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx (deepmerge-ts stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs, 6 high advisories), patched in 8.0.0. Reached only transitively, through obsidian-integration-testing -> webdriverio -> @wdio/config / @wdio/utils / webdriver, and no direct bump gets there: every wdio package still declares deepmerge-ts@^7.0.3, the newest release included. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades obsidian-integration-testing from 12.x to 1.1.2, and a downgrade is never an acceptable way to clear an advisory. The forced major is safe for these consumers. 8.0.0 breaks by renaming the mergeInfo system and aligning the customization shorthand, and a scan of the whole installed tree found only two bindings in use, `deepmerge` and `deepmergeCustom`. Both `deepmergeCustom` shapes present were run against 7.1.6 and 8.0.1 and produce identical output: @wdio/config's `mergeArrays` handler, which reads `meta.key` and returns `utils.actions.defaultMerge`, and webdriver's `deepmergeCustom({ mergeArrays: false })`. Mirrors the same override in create-obsidian-plugin's ADVISORY_OVERRIDES.
deepmerge-ts.manualCheck: The check reads the range @wdio/utils declares, not a version, because that range is what forces the override. When it moves to ^8 or later the override and this entry can both go. Before lifting it, re-run the deepmergeCustom probe rather than trusting the range alone: @wdio/config passes a handler that reads `meta.key`, and that is precisely the API 8.0.0 renamed, so a regression there would be silent rather than a crash.

fflate.why: Clears GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98 (fflate unzipSync infinite loop on malformed ZIP64 archives, 2 moderate advisories), which covers 0.7.0-0.7.4 and is fixed in 0.7.5. satori - a devDependency of the Astro docs site - pins fflate to the exact vulnerable 0.7.3 and is itself already latest, so only an override reaches it. fflate is ALSO a direct dependency now: the demo-vault archiver (src/script-utils/demo-vault.ts) writes release archives with its zipSync, and the desktop-zip-extractor and demo-vault-opener suites write their fixtures with it. So the override carries the `$fflate` shorthand, which keeps the forced version equal to the declared one by construction and collapses the tree onto that single copy. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades satori to 0.32.0, and a downgrade is never an acceptable way to clear an advisory.
fflate.manualCheck: The check reads satori's own declared pin, not a version, because that exact pin is what makes the OVERRIDE necessary - the direct dependency stays either way. When satori moves to 0.7.5 or later, or off fflate entirely, the override and this entry can both go while the `fflate` line in dependencies remains. Two paths verify a change: `npm run test:coverage` covers the archiver and the ZIP fixtures, and `npm run docs:build` covers satori's OG-image path, which lint and unit tests never touch.

js-yaml.why: js-yaml@5 drops the default export, so forcing it breaks `npm run docs:build` at Astro's own `import yaml from 'js-yaml'`. Lint and unit tests stay green, so only the docs build catches it. Held at the newest 4.x, which is the `v4-legacy` dist-tag - and that tag is where the advisory fixes are backported, so it is also what clears them for astro, starlight, cosmiconfig, markdownlint-cli2 and @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config at once: 4.3.1 carried CVE-2026-59870 (GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj, quadratic CPU in !!omap resolution) and 4.3.2 carries GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (maxTotalMergeKeys does not limit CPU use for empty merge sources, >=4.0.0 <4.3.2). The check tracks that tag rather than astro's declared range because of how the second one surfaced: on 2026-09-09 the sweep failed on it, since 4.3.2 had shipped while this exact pin - invisible to the caret sweep by construction - sat on 4.3.1, and the old astro-range check stayed green the whole time. A check that cannot see the condition it guards is the silent pin that machine-re-checking every pin exists to stop.
js-yaml.manualCheck: The check is a re-examination trigger, not proof: a newer v4-legacy publish means read its changelog and move this pin onto it, because while astro is on 4.x a backport is the only way an advisory leaves this tree. The override's DELETION condition is separate and has no mechanical test here - it can go once nothing needs js-yaml 4, i.e. when `node -e "process.stdout.write(require('astro/package.json').dependencies['js-yaml'])"` stops reporting ^4.3.0. Verify either change with `npm run docs:build`, the only gate that exercises Astro's default import.

smol-toml.why: Clears GHSA-7w5x-hrqm-74c2 (smol-toml denial of service via malformed TOML documents, <=1.7.0), fixed in 1.7.1. No direct bump reaches it: markdownlint-cli2 pins smol-toml at the exact vulnerable 1.7.0 and is itself already latest, while astro and @astrojs/internal-helpers declare ^1.6.0 but deduped onto that same 1.7.0 copy - so only an override moves all three at once. The forced version is not a hopeful one: cspell-config-lib requires ^1.8.0 and already had 1.8.0 installed alongside them in this tree, so the override collapses the two copies into one rather than introducing anything, and 1.8.0 is a minor inside 1.x. Caret rather than exact because nothing here needs an upper bound - it is an advisory floor, so the sweep floats it like any other caret. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades markdownlint-cli2 to 0.21.0, and a downgrade is never an acceptable way to clear an advisory.
smol-toml.manualCheck: The check reads markdownlint-cli2's own exact pin, not a version, because that pin is what makes the override necessary - the astro side would resolve fresh on its own. When it moves to 1.7.1 or later the override and this entry can both go. Two paths verify a change: `npm run lint:md` runs markdownlint-cli2, and `npm run docs:build` runs astro's config loading, which is where the other copy is read.

typescript.why: @typescript-eslint peer-requires >=4.8.4 <6.1.0, and its parser crashes on the TypeScript 7 (tsgo) native API, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7. TypeScript 7 was adopted in db7c417c and rolled back in 846d6c6a; 3234c7d0 made the pin exact so a dependency sweep could not drift it back. Propagates to the whole tree via overrides.typescript = $typescript.
